lines: Sixteen knobs sent out as one polyphonic cable, with a scale knob and an offset knob acting on every channel.
Sets the voltage of that channel of the output, 0-10V, or -10V to +10V when the menu sets the knobs bipolar.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16.
Multiplies every channel knob before the offset is added, -2 to +2.
Adds a fixed voltage to every channel after the scale knob, -10V to +10V.
Carries one channel per knob, each knob voltage multiplied by the scale knob and then offset.
Menu — Main Knob Range — Unipolar sets the sixteen channel knobs to 0-10V and Bipolar sets them to -10V to +10V.
Sixteen buttons sent out as one polyphonic cable, each button choosing between an off voltage and an on voltage.
Sends the off voltage while it is up and the on voltage while it is pressed, 0V and 10V until the menu or the A and B inputs change them.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16, or automatic at the far left, which follows the greater of the A and B channel counts.
Sets the voltage sent by a button that is up; a monophonic cable sets it for every channel and a polyphonic cable sets it channel by channel.
Sets the voltage sent by a button that is pressed down; a monophonic cable sets it for every channel and a polyphonic cable sets it channel by channel.
Carries one channel per button, each at its off or on voltage.
Menu — Exclusive Mode (like radio buttons: only can be pressed at a time) — pressing one button releases the rest.
Menu — Momentary (gate output while button is held) — a button sends its on voltage only while it is held down.
Menu — Off / On Values (A ... B) — picks the pair of voltages the buttons send: 0-10V, -5V to +5V, 0-5V, 0-1V, -1V to +1V, or -10V to +10V.
Polyphonic voltmeter, sample and hold and random voltage source: sixteen values are shown on the display and sent out of one polyphonic cable.
Acts as one clock event for the active clock mode, updating the values by hand.
Clears all sixteen displayed and output values to 0V.
Picks which channel of the clock input is read in Single-Channel clock mode.
Picks which channel of the value input is read in Single-Channel input mode.
Steps the input mode through Single-Channel, reading one chosen channel of the value input; Internal, random voltages made inside the module; and Polyphonic, each value channel feeding its own line.
Steps the clock mode through Single-Channel, reading one chosen channel of the clock input; Internal, updating at audio rate with no clock; and Polyphonic, each clock channel updating its own line.
A trigger updates the displayed and output values; in Polyphonic clock mode each channel updates the line of the same number.
The signal being measured or sampled; in Polyphonic input mode each channel feeds the line of the same number.
A trigger clears all sixteen displayed and output values to 0V.
Carries the sixteen displayed values, one per polyphonic channel.
Menu — Random Generator Range — sets the voltages used by Internal input mode and by Rack's Randomize: 0-10V, -5V to +5V, 0-5V, 0-1V, -1V to +1V, -10V to +10V, -2V to +2V, or 0-2V.
Menu — Show Clock Blinkers — turns the clock activity marks behind the display lines on or off.
Menu — Visual — holds Bar Mode, set to Unipolar or Bipolar, and sliders for Text Opacity and Bars Opacity.
Menu — Clock Mode — Single-Channel, Internal or Polyphonic, the same setting as the clock mode button on the panel.
Menu — Input Mode — Single-Channel, Internal or Polyphonic, the same setting as the input mode button on the panel.
Menu — Theme — picks the colours the display is drawn in: Boldy, Poloneck, Hut, Typhus, Moss, Check, Gratings, Ant or Santana.
Note — four small marks are printed beside the top of the display, reading TXT, UNI, SVL and Thm; left-clicking one opens its own menu for the visual mode, the bar mode, the opacities and the theme.
computerscare-debug.notes: The value input carries whatever is being measured, so it is left without a family.

lines: Four channels of attenuversion, offset and microtonal quantisation, each with an unquantised and a quantised output.
Shifts the quantised output by whole scale steps, from an octave down to an octave up.
Sets how many equal divisions the octave is split into, 1 to 24, with 12 giving ordinary semitones.
Attenuates and inverts the range CV of that column, -1 to +1.
Multiplies the input signal of that column, -2 to +2, with the attenuverted range CV added to it first.
Attenuates and inverts the offset CV of that column, -1 to +1.
Adds a fixed voltage to that column after the range section, -10V to +10V.
The signal that column attenuverts, offsets and quantises.
Adds to the range knob of that column through the small range attenuverter, modulating the multiplication applied to the input.
Adds to the offset knob of that column through the small offset attenuverter.
The column's input multiplied by the range setting and shifted by the offset setting, with no quantisation.
The attenuverted and offset signal snapped to the programmed scale, the input range spread equally between the allowed notes rather than each note taking the voltages nearest it.
Note — the scale is typed into the text field as the number of steps from each note to the next, so 43 gives a major triad and 221222 a major scale; the closing step back to the root is implied.
Menu — Scale Presets — types a scale into the text field: Major, Natural Minor, the two pentatonics, Blues, Chromatic, Harmonic Minor, Whole-Tone, Whole-Half Diminished, and seven chord shapes.
Menu — Gain Mode — sets one column to Bipolar, where a negative effective gain inverts the input, or to VCA Mode (Unipolar Gain), where the gain and both outputs are clamped at 0.
Note — the text field comes up holding 221222, an ordinary major scale, so the quantised outputs work before anything is typed.
Menu — Set All To Bipolar — puts all four columns into bipolar gain at once, and Set All To Unipolar puts all four into VCA mode.
A ten by ten patch matrix holding sixteen scenes, a clock stepping through whole sets of connections.
Sets how many scenes the sequence steps through, 1 to 16.
Advances to the next scene by hand.
Moves the editing scene on by one, cycling through all sixteen whatever the step count is set to.
Moves the editing scene back by one, cycling through all sixteen whatever the step count is set to.
Connects that input jack to that output jack; a green light marks the connection in the scene being edited and a red light marks it in the scene playing now.
Returns the sequence to scene 1.
A trigger advances to the next scene, returning to scene 1 after the last one.
A signal fed into the matrix, reaching whichever output jacks are connected to it in the active scene.
A trigger randomises the matrix, following the randomisation choices on the menu.
A trigger returns the sequence to scene 1.
The sum of every input connected to it in the active scene.
Menu — Only Randomize Active Connections — limits randomisation to rows with a cable in the input jack and columns with a cable in the output jack.
Menu — Which Step to Randomize — Edit step randomises the scene being edited, Active step the scene playing now, and All steps all sixteen.
Menu — Output Row Randomization Method — sets how many inputs randomisation gives an output: One or none, Exactly one, Zero or more, or One or more.
Menu — Output Polyphony — sets how many channels every output carries, 1 to 16, or Automatic.
Note — every connection in all sixteen scenes starts switched off, so nothing reaches any output until matrix buttons are pressed or the matrix is randomised.
computerscare-fatherandson.notes: Output Row Randomization Method draws with fixed probabilities in the source: One or none takes a single input at 70 percent, Zero or more takes each input at 20 percent, and One or more takes one input plus each of the rest at 20 percent.

lines: Six trigger sequencers programmed as text, each row typed as the number of clocks from one trigger to the next.
Advances every row by one step.
Returns every row to the start of its pattern.
Forces that row to restart its pattern on the next clock, which is how a newly typed pattern takes effect without waiting for the old one to finish.
A trigger advances every row that has no cable in its own clock input.
A trigger returns every row that has no cable in its own reset input to the start of its pattern.
A trigger advances that row by one step, and a cable here makes the row ignore the global clock.
A trigger returns that row to the start of its pattern, and a cable here makes the row ignore the global reset.
Sends 10V on the steps that row's pattern calls for, with one polyphonic channel per pattern where the text sets more than one.
Sends a trigger on the first step of that row's pattern.
Note — a pattern is a string of step lengths: 2 triggers every second clock, 31 triggers on the 1st and 4th of every four, and 0 is a rest.
Note — angle brackets hold a step length above 9, and @8 forces the pattern to repeat every 8 clocks whatever its own length is.
Note — semicolons split a row into separate patterns for separate polyphonic channels, the hash character stands for the channel number, and arithmetic can be used wherever a length is expected.
Note — a red display means a newly typed pattern is waiting for the running one to come back to its first step.
Note — the six text fields start empty and no row sends anything until a pattern is typed into its field; click the field and type, for example 2 to trigger every second clock.
Menu — Set All Channels Polyphony — sets every row's output to Automatic or to a fixed 1 to 16 channels.
Menu — Channel 1 Polyphony — sets that row's output to Automatic or to a fixed 1 to 16 channels; there is one such item per row, Channel 1 through Channel 6.
Six CV sequencers programmed as text, each step of a row naming one of twenty-six knobs, one of twenty-six inputs, or an exact voltage.
Sets the voltage sent when a row's pattern reaches its lowercase letter, 0-10V.
Advances every row by one step.
Returns every row to the start of its pattern.
Forces that row to restart its pattern on the next clock, which is how a newly typed pattern takes effect without waiting for the old one to finish.
A trigger advances every row that has no cable in its own clock input.
A trigger returns every row that has no cable in its own reset input to the start of its pattern.
A trigger advances that row by one step, and a cable here makes the row ignore the global clock.
A trigger returns that row to the start of its pattern, and a cable here makes the row ignore the global reset.
The voltage passed on when a row's pattern reaches its uppercase letter.
Carries the voltage of the step that row has reached, held until the next step.
Sends a trigger on the first step of that row's pattern.
Note — abcd steps through knobs a, b, c and d and then repeats, angle brackets hold an exact voltage such as 4.20, and @8 runs a sequence for 8 steps before looping.
Note — curly braces pick one of the enclosed values at random on each clock, and empty braces pick from all twenty-six knobs.
Note — square brackets around comma-separated sequences run each sequence in turn for the number of steps given after the @ sign.
Note — the six text fields start empty and no row sends anything until a pattern is typed into its field; click the field and type, for example abcd to step through knobs a, b, c and d.
Menu — Wiggle Knobs — moves the twenty-six knobs a little way from where they are, leaving the text fields as they are.
Menu — Randomize Text Fields — replaces the six patterns with randomly built ones, leaving the knobs as they are.
Menu — Knob Range — sets the range of the twenty-six knobs: 0-10V, 0-5V, 0-2V, 0-1V, -10V to +10V, -5V to +5V, -2V to +2V, or -1V to +1V.
Re-routes the channels of a polyphonic cable, each output channel taking whichever input channel is chosen for it.
Picks which input channel that output channel carries, 1 to 16; a channel above the input's channel count gives 0V.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16, or automatic at the far left, which matches the input's channel count.
The polyphonic signal whose channels are re-routed.
Takes the routing knobs over, each 0.667V stepping on to the next input channel and wrapping round after sixteen; a monophonic cable routes every output channel from one input channel.
Carries the re-routed channels.
Menu — Randomize one-to-one (Don't re-use input channels on randomize) — makes Rack's Randomize shuffle the routing so that every input channel is used exactly once.
Menu — Set All To — points every one of the sixteen routing knobs at the same input channel, chosen from Set all to ch. 1 through Set all to ch. 16.
Rotates the channels of a polyphonic cable and sets how many channels come out, with a display and a CV output of the input's channel count. Superseded by Toly Pools v2.
Rotates the channels of the input, 0 to 15, so a setting of 1 sends input channel 2 out on channel 1 and so on round the sixteen channels.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16.
The polyphonic signal whose channels are rotated.
Takes the rotation knob over while a cable is patched, 0.625V per channel of rotation, and a negative voltage counts down from sixteen.
Takes the output channel count knob over while a cable is patched, 0.625V per channel.
Carries the rotated channels.
A voltage for the number of channels on the input, 0.625V per channel, so sixteen channels gives 10V.
Rotates the channels of a polyphonic cable and sets how many channels come out, with a display and a CV output of the input's channel count.
Rotates the channels of the input, -16 to +16, so a setting of 1 sends input channel 2 out on channel 1 and so on; the rotation CV is added to it.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16, or automatic at the far left, which matches the input's channel count; the channel count CV is added to it.
The polyphonic signal whose channels are rotated.
Adds to the rotation knob, one channel of rotation for every 0.625V.
Adds to the output channel count knob, one channel for every 0.625V.
Carries the rotated channels.
A voltage for the number of channels on the input, 0.625V per channel, so sixteen channels gives 10V.
Menu — Rotation Mode — sets what the rotation wraps around, as Repeat Input Channels, Rotate Through Maximum of Output, Input Channels, or Rotate Through 16 Channels (Legacy).
Steps through the channels of a polyphonic input one channel at a time, a polyphonic clock giving several independent sequences at once.
Advances every sequence by one channel.
Returns every sequence to the first channel.
Sets how many independent sequences run, 1 to 16, or automatic at the far left, which follows the greater of the clock and reset channel counts.
The polyphonic signal whose channels are stepped through.
A trigger moves a sequence on to the next channel of the input, wrapping round after the last channel; each channel of a polyphonic clock drives its own sequence.
A trigger returns a sequence to the first channel of the input; a monophonic cable resets every sequence, and reset channels beyond the clock's channel count are ignored.
Carries the channel each sequence has reached, one polyphonic channel per sequence.
Sends 10V on the clock that brings a sequence back to the first channel of the input.
Draws a face from the voltages of a polyphonic input, one feature per channel.
Attenuates and inverts the input before it is drawn, -2 to +2.
Adds a fixed voltage to the input before it is drawn, -5V to +5V.
Shuffles which input channel draws which part of the face, a different shuffle at each setting from -10 to +10.
The signal drawn as a face, a polyphonic cable giving each channel its own feature.
Menu — Face Emits Light — draws the face on Rack's light layer so that it glows when the room is dark; turned off, the face is drawn as ordinary panel art.
computerscare-foly-pace.notes: The Time parameter has no control on the panel and is left without a line.

lines: Draws a stick figure from the voltages of a polyphonic input, one limb per channel.
Attenuates and inverts the input before it is drawn, -2 to +2.
Adds a fixed voltage to the input before it is drawn, -5V to +5V.
Shuffles which input channel draws which part of the figure, a different shuffle at each setting from -10 to +10.
The signal drawn as a stick figure, a polyphonic cable giving each channel its own limb.
Menu — Stick Figure Emits Light — draws the figure on Rack's light layer so that it glows when the room is dark; turned off, it is drawn as ordinary panel art.
computerscare-stoly-fick-pigure.notes: The Time parameter has no control on the panel and is left without a line.

lines: A resizable blank panel showing a fixed image or an animated GIF, loaded from disk, dropped onto the module, or run as a slideshow.
Note — nothing is shown until an image is loaded, either through Load image on the menu or by dropping a PNG, JPEG, BMP or GIF file onto the module.
Menu — Load image (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF) — opens a file chooser, and the path of the file in use is printed under it.
Menu — Image Scaling — Fit Both (stretch both directions), Fit Width, Fit Height or Free.
Menu — Animation Enabled — turns GIF playback on or off.
Menu — Animation Options — holds Animation Mode, set to Forward, Reverse, Ping Pong, Random Shuffled or Full Random, a Constant Frame Delay toggle, and an Animation Speed slider.
Menu — Slideshow Enabled — loads another file from the current image's directory over and over.
Menu — Slideshow Options — holds the next-file order, Shuffle Seed, Slideshow Time, a Crossfade Enabled toggle and Crossfade Time.
Menu — Keyboard Controls — lists the shortcuts, and carries the Invert Y-Axis toggle that reverses which way the image moves.
Menu — Dim Visuals with Room — makes the image follow Rack's room brightness; turned off, the image stays fully opaque as the lights go down.
Menu — Hide panel — removes the blank panel art that is drawn when no image is loaded.
Note — drag either side edge of the module to make it wider or narrower.
Note — with the mouse over the module, A, S, D and W move the image, Z and X zoom it, and Q and E rotate it by a quarter turn.
Note — with the mouse over the module, J and L step one frame back and forward, K goes to the first frame and I to a random frame.
Note — with the mouse over the module, P turns the animation on and off, M turns the slideshow on and off, and the two square bracket keys load the previous and next file in the directory.
Expander for Custom Blank, placed immediately to its left, giving clock control of the GIF animation and triggers out as it runs.
Steps the clock mode through Sync, synchronising the animation to a steady clock; Scan, where 0-10V picks the frame from first to last; and Frame, one frame advanced per clock.
Returns the animation to its first frame.
Sets which frame counts as the first one for the reset input, the end-of-animation output and the ping pong turning point.
Loads the next slideshow file, in the order chosen in Custom Blank's own menu.
Drives the animation in the way the clock mode sets: a steady clock to synchronise to, a 0-10V scan across the frames, or one frame advanced per trigger.
A trigger returns the animation to its first frame.
A trigger loads the next slideshow file, in the order chosen in Custom Blank's own menu.
Sends a trigger each time the animation restarts.
Sends a trigger each time the frame changes.
Note — the expander does nothing unless a Custom Blank is the module immediately to its right, and that Custom Blank has an animated GIF loaded.
Menu — Sync, Scan and Frame Advance — on the clock mode switch's own right-click menu rather than the module's, each with a line saying what that mode does.
computerscare-blank-expander.notes: The sync input takes a clock in two of the three modes and a 0-10V scan in the third, so it is left without a family.

lines: Generates a constant polyphonic voltage, the channels following one of five shapes across the polyphony.
Steps the shape through Linear, Sigmoid, Hump, Sinusoid and Pseudo-Random.
Moves the shape along the channels, -1 to +1, a whole pass of the polyphony at each extreme.
Sets how steeply the shape changes from one channel to the next, -2 to +2, with negative settings reversing it.
Multiplies the shape, -20 to +20, setting how far apart the channel voltages spread.
Adds a fixed voltage to every channel, -10V to +10V.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16.
Carries the generated voltages, one per polyphonic channel.
Menu — Display Color — a slider picking the colour of the bar display.
Menu — Algorithm — picks the shape spread across the channels: Linear, Sigmoid, Hump, Sinusoid or Pseudo-Random.
A sixteen by sixteen matrix mixer for one polyphonic cable, every input channel given its own level into every output channel.
Sets how much of that input channel reaches that output channel, -2 to +2.
Attenuates and inverts that input channel before the matrix, -2 to +2.
Attenuates and inverts that output channel after the matrix, -2 to +2.
Attenuates and inverts every output channel, -2 to +2, and attenuates the output trim CV when a cable is patched there.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16, or automatic at the far left, which matches the input's channel count.
Attenuates and inverts every input channel, -2 to +2, and attenuates the input trim CV when a cable is patched there.
Adds a fixed voltage to every input channel before the matrix, -10V to +10V.
Adds a fixed voltage to every output channel after the matrix, -10V to +10V.
The polyphonic signal fed into the matrix.
Scales every input channel, a tenth of its voltage multiplied by the input trim knob; a polyphonic cable scales each input channel separately.
Scales every output channel, a tenth of its voltage multiplied by the output trim knob; a polyphonic cable scales each output channel separately.
Carries the mixed channels.
Note — nothing is clipped, so large settings put hundreds of volts out; the global input and output attenuation knobs are what hold it in range.
Menu — Knob Color Mode — turns the colouring of the matrix knobs by their values on or off.
Menu — Knob Color Strength — a slider setting how strongly a matrix knob's value shows in its colour.
Menu — Knob Color Hue — a slider picking the hue the matrix knobs are coloured from.
Menu — Knob Fade — a slider setting how far a matrix knob at zero fades out.
Note — the matrix comes up with its diagonal at 1 and everything else at 0, so a fresh module passes each input channel straight through to the output channel of the same number.
A repeatable trigger and CV sequencer with no randomness in it: one knob picks the whole sequence, and the polyphonic channels can be spread away from that sequence.
Picks the trigger and CV sequence, 0 to 10, a small change giving a completely different sequence.
Attenuates and inverts the pattern CV, -1 to +1.
Sets how many steps the sequence has, 2 to 64.
Attenuates and inverts the step count CV, -1 to +1.
Sets how many of the steps carry a trigger, 0 percent giving none at all and 100 percent giving one on every clock.
Attenuates and inverts the density CV, -1 to +1.
Sets how many channels the outputs carry, 1 to 16, or automatic at the far left, which follows the greatest channel count among the clock and CV inputs.
Steps through Independent, each channel on its own sequence; Ch. 1 Trigger, all fired by channel 1; Trigger Cascade, each fired by the channel before; and EOC Cascade, by its end of cycle.
Returns every channel's sequence to its first step.
Sets how far the pattern changes from one polyphonic channel to the next, 0 percent giving every channel the same sequence.
Sets how the step count changes across the polyphonic channels, positive giving higher channels more steps and negative giving them fewer, down to two.
Sets how the density changes across the polyphonic channels, positive giving higher channels more triggers and negative giving them fewer.
Advances every channel's sequence by one step.
A trigger advances the sequences; each channel of a polyphonic clock drives its own sequence.
A trigger returns every sequence to its first step.
Adds to the pattern knob through the pattern attenuverter.
Adds to the step count knob through the step count attenuverter.
Adds to the density knob through the density attenuverter.
Sends 10V on the steps the sequence calls for, either as a copy of the clock pulse or as a gate whose length varies from step to step.
Sends 10V on the clock that brings a channel's sequence back to its first step.
Carries the sequence's voltage for the step it has reached, changing only on steps that trigger.
Carries a second voltage sequence on the same steps as the first, with its own scale, offset and variation.
Menu — CV 1 Configuration — holds CV Scale and CV Offset, which set the range of the CV output, and CV Variation, which changes its voltages while the trigger sequence stays as it was.
Menu — CV 2 Configuration — holds CV2 Scale, CV2 Offset and CV2 Variation, the same three settings for the CV2 output.
Menu — Gate Output Mode — switches the trigger output between a copy of the clock pulse and gates whose length varies from step to step.
Menu — Gate Length Configuration — holds Gate Length Scaling, Gate Length Minimum and Gate Length Variation, which set how long the gates run.
Menu — Polyphonic Triggering Mode — the same setting as the mode switch on the panel: Independent, Ch. 1 Trigger, Trigger Cascade or EOC Cascade.
Captures the Rack window or another visual source, blends two of them, transforms the result geometrically and in colour, and draws it back into its own display.
Freezes the capture on the frame showing when it is switched on; left off, the capture runs continuously.
Blends the two sources, -1 for source 1 on its own, 0 for an equal blend and +1 for source 2 on its own.
Turns that transform row on or off.
Attenuates and inverts the CV feeding that transform row.
Zooms the image evenly, 0.1 to 4.0, with each volt of CV worth 0.3.
Stretches the image horizontally, -5 to +5 mapped exponentially, negative settings mirroring it, with each volt of CV worth 0.5.
Stretches the image vertically, -5 to +5 mapped exponentially, negative settings mirroring it, with each volt of CV worth 0.5.
Rotates the image about the centre of the display, -180 to +180 degrees and wrapping beyond that, with each volt of CV worth 36 degrees.
Sets the kaleidoscope in whole steps from -12 to +12: 0 is off, positive values give flower rotational symmetry and negative values give two- and four-part kaleidoscopes.
Moves the image sideways by -1 to +1 of the image width and wraps round, with each volt of CV worth 0.1.
Moves the image up and down by -1 to +1 of the display height and wraps round, with each volt of CV worth 0.1.
Turns all the colours round the hue wheel, -360 to +360 degrees; positive moves them together and negative splits them and raises saturation and contrast, with each volt of CV worth 36 degrees.
Warps the colours, -1 to +1: positive posterises and crushes the contrast, negative solarises towards inversion, and full negative gives an inverted image, with each volt of CV worth 0.1.
A gate above 0.5V forces the freeze on and a low gate forces continuous capture, overriding the button.
Adds a fifth of its voltage to the mix knob, the result clamped to the -1 to +1 range.
A gate above 0.5V turns that transform row on and a low gate turns it off, overriding the row's button.
Modulates that transform row through the row's attenuverter.
Note — with the mouse over the module, Q toggles edit mode and A cycles the mouse mapping between translate with scale on the wheel, and axis scale with rotation on the wheel.
Note — the module is resized by dragging its right edge, and an image file dropped onto it loads into source 2.
Menu — Source 1 — sets what the first source captures: Full Rack Window, Load image, Select rack rectangle, Select window rectangle or a chosen Module; Clear source empties it.
Menu — Fold Frequency — a slider under the Color Warp heading, raising the colour fold frequency from 1.0 to 4.0 and widening the chromatic divergence.
Menu — Algorithm — chooses whether the kaleidoscope runs before the translation or after it.
Menu — Minimize UI — strips the panel art, controls, labels and jack graphics so that only the display is left, holding the right edge in place.
Menu — Render as rack background — draws the visual behind the modules as well as in the display.
Menu — Transform when frozen — keeps the knobs and CV active on a frozen frame instead of freezing the transform settings along with it.
Menu — Visual — holds Tile empty space, Maintain aspect ratio and Crop Rack Window Borders.
Menu — Dim visuals with room — makes the render follow Rack's room brightness setting.
Menu — Blend mode — sets how the two sources are combined: Crossfade, Normal, Add, Subtract, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Difference, Darken, Lighten or XOR.
Menu — Full Rack BG — holds Empty module window, which leaves the display itself transparent, and sliders for Backdrop Alpha, Backdrop Darken and Backdrop Blur.
Note — source 2 comes up set to an image with no file chosen, so the mix knob turned towards source 2 shows nothing until an image is loaded or dropped on.
Menu — Source 2 — sets what the second source captures, with the same items as Source 1; the menu item is printed with the source in use after the name.
computerscare-portaloof.notes: The Fold row's gate and CV inputs and its enable and attenuverter parameters have no control on the panel; the Fold Frequency slider is on the menu. The two source menu items are printed with the source in use after the name, as Source 1: Rack and Source 2: Image, so the name changes with the setting.

lines: Splits a polyphonic input across sixteen outputs, each output monophonic, polyphonic or silent according to the routing mode.
Steps the routing mode through Single, Dynamic Below, Dynamic Above and Custom.
The polyphonic signal being split.
A trigger randomises the stored custom routes, following the randomisation choices on the menu; each channel of a polyphonic trigger randomises the matching output.
Carries the input channels that the active routing mode gives it, as a monophonic or a polyphonic signal.
Note — in Single mode each output carries the input channel of its own number, on its own.
Note — in Dynamic Below a connected output carries the input channels from its own number as far as the next connected output, running to the end of the input's channels when there is no later one.
Note — in Dynamic Above a connected output carries the input channels from the previous connected output as far as its own number.
Note — in Custom mode each output carries its stored route, which can hold anything from no input channels to all sixteen.
Note — in Custom mode, clicking an output's row opens that route for editing, where the yellow boxes are the input channels it carries.
Note — in Custom mode, right-clicking an output's row opens a field where its route is typed, with 1 to 9 for those channels, 0 for channel 10, and a to f for channels 11 to 16.
Menu — Set Custom Routing to — copies the Single, Dynamic Below or Dynamic Above routing into the stored custom routes without changing the mode in use.
Menu — Input Pool — sets which input channels randomisation may draw from in Custom mode: Only active input channels or All input channels.
Menu — Routing Mode — Single, Dynamic Below, Dynamic Above or Custom, the same setting as the mode button on the panel.
Menu — Replacement — sets how randomisation picks channels in Custom mode: With replacement, Without replacement or Shuffle existing.
Menu — Channel Count — sets how long a randomised route is in Custom mode: Same channels as current or Random channels.
Menu — Output Targets — sets which outputs randomisation changes in Custom mode: Only connected outputs or All outputs.
Runs one polyphonic signal through sixteen insert channels, each channel adding to it, replacing it, crossfading, multiplying, comparing or limiting it.
Attenuates and inverts the main input before the inserts, -2 to +2.
Adds a fixed voltage to the main input before the inserts, -10V to +10V.
Sets how many channels the output carries, 1 to 16, or automatic at the far left, which follows the greater of the input's channel count and the furthest patched or normalled insert.
Scales that channel's insert input, and in Crossfade mode sets the blend between the main signal and the insert.
Offsets that channel: in most modes it shifts the final voltage; in Minimum, Maximum and Compare it shifts the insert side before the comparison, and alone sets the clamp level or threshold.
The polyphonic signal run through the sixteen insert channels.
The signal that channel's mode works on, taken through that channel's attenuverter and offset.
Carries the processed signal.
Note — each channel's mode button steps through Add, Insert, Crossfade, VCA bipolar, VCA unipolar, Minimum, Maximum and Compare; Compare puts out a clean 0V or 10V, and nothing else is clipped.
Menu — Set all to — gives all sixteen insert channels the same mode at once.
Menu — Insert normalization — sets the insert inputs as independent, or lets a polyphonic insert fill the channels after it.
Menu — Main Input Polyphonic Wrap Mode — sets how the main input's channels are mapped when the output carries more channels than the input.
Menu — Multiple inserts break normalization — makes a later patched insert stop an earlier one's polyphonic normalling from reaching past it.
